jobs.occupation: PhD in Boreal Raptor Ecology under Climate Change
jobs.description:
Department of Wildlife, Fish, and Environmental Studies
Research subject:
Biology
Description of the doctoral project
Boreal Raptors – Understanding and Predicting the Dynamics of Mountain Raptor Communities under Climate Change
Why do some raptor species thrive while others decline as northern ecosystems become warmer? We are seeking a motivated PhD student to join the Boreal Raptor Project to investigate how climate, prey dynamics, landscape changes and interactions among species shape raptor communities in mountain and boreal forest ecosystems.
The project combines long-term monitoring data from northern Sweden and the Scandinavian mountains with new field observations and quantitative ecological modelling. We will examine variation in species occurrence, breeding phenology, reproductive success and distribution, and investigate how these patterns can be used to predict changes under future climate and land-use scenarios.
The research may include eagles, falcons, hawks and other raptors characteristic of northern ecosystems, as well as ecological interactions with species such as ravens.
Key questions include how weather, snow conditions and prey populations influence different raptor species, why species differ in their responses, and how forestry, infrastructure and other landscape changes interact with climate-driven processes. Specific research questions will be developed jointly with the PhD student.
About the position
Research tasks
The PhD student will analyse existing long-term datasets and newly collected information on species occurrence, breeding territories, reproductive success and environmental conditions.
The research will involve advanced statistical and spatial modelling, potentially including generalised linear mixed models, hierarchical models, occupancy and population models, time-series analysis and community ecology approaches. GIS and remote sensing will be used to quantify changes in climate, snow cover, vegetation and land use.
Fieldwork in mountain and boreal forest environments may include breeding territory surveys, reproductive monitoring and collection of complementary ecological data.
An important objective is to move beyond describing historical patterns towards developing models capable of predicting future ecological changes.
Requirements
Eligibility
Applicants must hold a second-cycle (Master's) degree, have completed at least 240 higher education credits, including 60 credits at second-cycle level, or have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge through other means in Sweden or abroad (Swedish Higher Education Ordinance, Chapter 7, Section 39).
English proficiency equivalent to English B/6 in the Swedish upper-secondary school system is required.
Your profile
We seek candidates with a Master's degree or equivalent in ecology, biology, wildlife ecology, conservation biology, zoology or a related discipline.
Applicants should have experience in quantitative ecological analysis and statistical modelling, proficiency in R or a comparable programming environment, and a strong interest in population and community ecology and ecological responses to environmental change.
The ability to work independently and collaboratively within a research team is essential.
Excellent spoken and written English is required, as the position involves scientific writing, presentations and collaboration in an international research environment.
Additional merits include experience in raptor or avian ecology, analysis of long-term ecological datasets, hierarchical or demographic modelling, spatial ecology, GIS, remote sensing and ecological fieldwork.
We particularly value scientific curiosity, analytical thinking and the ability to formulate independent ecological research questions rather than simply applying existing analytical methods.
About us
The Department of Wildlife, Fish and Environmental Studies at the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) in Umeå conducts internationally recognised research in wildlife ecology, conservation biology, restoration ecology and quantitative ecology.
The PhD student will join an active international research environment with opportunities to collaborate with researchers, government agencies and organisations working on the monitoring and conservation of northern raptor populations.
We offer a fully funded four-year PhD position, training in advanced ecological modelling, opportunities for fieldwork and participation in scientific conferences and international research networks.
Learn more about working at SLU: https://www.slu.se/om-slu/jobba-pa-slu/
Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/.

jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Urban Water Engineering
jobs.description:
Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? As a doctoral student with us, you will work closely with leading researchers in a strong, international research environment, with access to advanced laboratory equipment and solid funding opportunities. You will be offered secure employment, high-quality supervision, and room to grow, both as a researcher and as a person.
The Urban Water Engineering research group at the Department of Civil, Environmental and Natural resources engineering at Luleå University of Technology seeks a driven and committed PhD student to investigate how smart monitoring and predictive modelling can support more effective and environmentally sustainable maintenance of urban drainage infrastructure. The research focuses on understanding sediment accumulation through sensor-based monitoring and data analysis, contributing to improved water quality and urban flood resilience. More information on http://www.ltu.se/water
Subject description
Urban Water Engineering encompasses the entire urban water system (storm drains, drinking water supply and wastewater) with respect to collection, transport and treatment, as well as organisation and planning. The research aims to encourage a strong economy, clean environment and the wise use of resources, while preserving the public’s health and safety.
Project description
Stormwater transports a wide range of pollutants from urban environments to receiving waters, posing major challenges for the protection of surface waters and coastal ecosystems. Urban drainage infrastructures, such as gully pots and stormwater ponds, play a critical role by retaining sediments and associated contaminants. However, their performance depends on effective operation and maintenance (O&M), which in practice is often reactive or based on fixed schedules, despite large spatial and temporal variability in sediment accumulation. This PhD project is part of a larger interdisciplinary research initiative aiming to enable a transition towards more data-driven and environmentally responsible maintenance of urban drainage infrastructures. The overall goal is to reduce pollutant loads to coastal and marine environments while supporting sustainable urban water management.
The PhD research will focus on developing a data-driven understanding of sediment accumulation processes in urban drainage infrastructures. This includes long-term monitoring using high-resolution sensors to capture sediment dynamics across rainfall events and seasons. Based on these data, predictive models will be developed to estimate sediment accumulation and infrastructure’s remaining functionality. The results will support more effective maintenance strategies by identifying when and where maintenances are needed to maximise environmental performance and operational efficiency.
Within this project, the doctoral student will be involved in collaboration with stakeholders in the water and wastewater industry and will communicate results both with the industry and international researchers through LTU's well-established competence network.
Duties
As a PhD student, you will perform both experimental and theoretical work. You will learn how to collect and analyse scientific data within your research area as well as communicate your results at national and international conferences and in scientific journals. Most of your working time will be devoted to your own research studies, including both research and coursework. In addition, you will also carry out departmental duties, such as teaching and/or assisting in other research projects. You will have two or three supervisors who support you in your work. The research work for this project will specifically include experimental work.
Qualifications
We seek a candidate with an MSc degree or equivalent or fully completed course requirements of at least 240 ETCS of which at least 60 ETCS are at an advanced level or equivalent. The degree should be within the field of water and environment, environmental engineering, natural resources engineering, civil engineering, or equivalent. Specific knowledge of stormwater management, hydraulics/hydrology, statistics, machine learning, thermodynamics (e.g. heat transfer processes) and programming, as well as experience of sensor-based monitoring, are meritorious. Other important skills are the ability to work independently and take initiative, as well as being able to explore new research areas.
English language skills are required since the results will be presented internationally in scientific journals and at conferences. Swedish/Scandinavian language skills are beneficial, as they will facilitate communication with stakeholders and participation in teaching activities. Having a driver’s license is meritorious, as it will facilitate research work.
Applicants should provide contact details to minimum two reference persons upon request.
For further information about a specific subject see:
* http://www.ltu.se/research/Utbildning-pa-forskarniva/Studieplaner/Allmanna-studieplaner-Teknisk-fakultetsnamnd?l=en

Employment as a PhD student is limited to 4 years, teaching and other department duties may be added to that time with max 20%. Placement: Luleå. Starting: Spring 2027.

Collaborate across multidisciplinary R&D teams to achieve product development milestones.

Participate in technical discussions, troubleshooting activities, and scientific reviews.

Support the transfer of product specifications and knowledge to internal stakeholders.

Qualifications

You are proactive, structured and solution-oriented, with a genuine interest in providing great customer service. You enjoy taking ownership, working both independently and as part of a team, and switching between customer conversations and written content tasks.
You do not need to be a developer, but you should be comfortable learning digital systems, investigating problems and finding practical solutions.
Requirements
Fluent Dutch, both written and spoken, with excellent spelling, grammar and the ability to adapt your tone for different audiences.
Strong English skills, both written and spoken.
Previous Customer Service experience, preferably within e-commerce or a digital environment.
Strong technical aptitude and confidence working across multiple digital systems.
Good problem-solving skills, attention to detail and a structured way of working.
Ability to maintain high service quality in a fast-paced environment.
Confidence in writing, editing and proofreading customer-facing content in Dutch.

Nice to Have
Experience with Zendesk, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central or Centra.
Technical troubleshooting experience within e-commerce.
Experience with automation, AI-supported customer service tools or similar technologies.
Additional languages: Swedish, German and/or French.
Previous experience with translation, localization, newsletters or e-commerce copywriting.

Employment: Full-time (100%), fixed-term maternity cover, March 2027 – August 2028, with the possibility of extension.

Location: Stockholm
We look forward to hearing from you!

Job Description

At IKEA, the product range is our identity. Every textile product we create should be safe, compliant, affordable and designed for the many people. 
As legislation, standards and customer expectations continue to evolve, we need people who are curious about what comes next and motivated by turning complexity into opportunities.
That's why we're looking for a Product Requirement Specialist within Textiles to join us on our journey. 
As a Product Requirement Specialist (PRS), you help IKEA understand and prepare for existing and future product coordinating stakeholders in relevant working groups and forums, e.g. PRIO groups. Be responsible to influence, relevant to the IKEA range, new and existing legislations, regulations, and standards, within assigned area(s) and when relevant, to maintain a network of stakeholders in external alliances, e.g. standardization, organizations and academia. 
You will work closely with colleagues across the value chain while building networks with external stakeholders, including standardization organizations and industry partners. Through these collaborations, you will contribute to influencing legislation, regulations, and standards relevant to the IKEA range. 
If you are energized by understanding what is happening beyond today's requirements and curious about how future developments may shape tomorrow's products, this could be the role for you. 
You are passionate about textiles and motivated by helping others understand complex topics. 
We believe you have: 

University degree in Textile Engineering or Textile Technology 

Knowledge of textile materials and relevant standards, regulations, or product requirements. 

Experience from product development, requirement management, compliance, or another relevant part of the value chain. 

Strong analytical skills and the ability to assess and interpret complex topics. 

The ability to communicate complex issues in a clear and engaging way. 

Experience collaborating with many stakeholders and building strong networks. 

Fluency in English, both written and spoken. 

Most importantly, you are curious, collaborative, and driven by continuous learning. You want to use your expertise to make a difference and contribute to a better everyday life for the many people. 

Additional Information

At IKEA, you'll have the opportunity to combine deep specialist knowledge with collaboration, learning, and influence. You'll join a global environment where your expertise helps us understand change, prepare for the future, and continuously improve the way we develop our products. 
If you're passionate about textiles, fascinated by how requirements shape products, and excited by the opportunity to influence what comes next, we'd love to hear from you. 
This is a permanent position and it´s placed in Älmhult, Sweden.   
We look forward to receiving your application – CV and answer to the below question – in English latest by November 15, 2026.  
• What made you interested in this role and enticed you to apply?   
• What experience do you have that you believe will be beneficial for you in this role?

jobs.occupation: Teacher Librarian, Bladins International School of Malmö
jobs.description:
At Bladins International School of Malmö (BISM), we are looking for an enthusiastic Teacher Librarian to join our Primary Years Programme (PYP) and Middle Years Programme (MYP) in January 2027.
If you are passionate about inspiring a love of reading, developing information literacy and supporting learning in an international school, we would love to hear from you.
About Bladins International School of Malmö
BISM is an IB Continuum School in central Malmö, offering the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and Middle Years Programme (MYP) to approximately 360 students from diverse nationalities and cultures.
As part of Bladins Foundation, a non-profit educational organisation, we provide a supportive, internationally minded learning environment where students grow into knowledgeable, caring and responsible global citizens.
The Role
As Teacher Librarian, you will promote reading, inquiry-based learning and students' research, information literacy and critical thinking skills across PYP and MYP.
BISM has two dedicated libraries, one for PYP and one for MYP. You will develop these as welcoming and inclusive learning spaces and work closely with teachers to support learning across the curriculum.
Key responsibilities include:

Developing and managing both school libraries and their print and digital collections

Promoting reading for pleasure through library lessons, initiatives and events

Teaching information literacy, research skills, digital literacy and critical thinking

Collaborating with teachers to support PYP units of inquiry and MYP subjects, with awareness of the curriculum across MYP

Supporting students' Approaches to Learning (ATL) skills, including ethical use of information, referencing and academic integrity

Ensuring resources reflect the school's international, multilingual community and diverse learning needs

Building positive relationships with students, colleagues and families and engaging with the wider BISM community

Contributing to school development and a welcoming library environment

Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for a qualified, proactive Teacher Librarian with a passion for literacy and student learning.
You are:

Qualified in library and information science, preferably with school library experience

Experienced in supporting children's and young people's reading, research and information literacy

Knowledgeable about children's and young adult literature and able to inspire readers of different ages

Skilled in inquiry-based learning and collaboration with classroom and subject teachers

Confident using digital library systems, educational technology and online resources

Inclusive, organised and able to manage library activities independently

A positive communicator and collaborative member of an international team

Committed to professional development

Experience with the International Baccalaureate (IB), particularly PYP and/or MYP, is an advantage. Understanding the IB philosophy, Learner Profile and Approaches to Learning (ATL) is highly valued.
As English is the school's working language, professional spoken and written English is required.
Why Join BISM?
At BISM, you will join a welcoming international community committed to students, colleagues and learning. We offer supportive colleagues, professional development, an IB learning environment and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference to students' development.
Employment Information
Position: Teacher Librarian  Employment type: Permanent employment, with a six-month probationary period  Working hours: Part-time (60%)  Start date: January 2027
Application
Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Please apply by 30 November 2026.
For more information, contact:
Kumari Nevill, Primary School Principal Kumari.nevill@bladins.se
We look forward to welcoming a colleague who shares our commitment to high-quality education, collaboration and student success.

Reports to: Middle School Principal
Our vision
To be recognised as a leading international school that inspires and educates generations of global change-makers.
Our mission
Stockholm International School inspires and educates children of the global community through internationally recognised learning programs. We enable international mobility and support growth and talent development in the Stockholm region and beyond.
Duties and Responsibilities: 
Teaching MYP 1 - Grade 6 to MYP 4 - Grade 9, and Primary Grades 4-5 French language acquisition.
Developing materials appropriate for classes with a wide range of abilities.
Contributing to the development and implementation of the curriculum.
Creating and implementing lessons for differentiated skill levels in a classroom.  
Communicating regularly with parents. 
Being an active and contributing member of the school’s faculty. 
Participating in the full range of professional activities in the school. 
Actively contributing to the operational needs of the school. 

Qualifications and Experience:
French language teaching qualification.
At least two years of experience as a teacher. 
Preferred experience with IB programmes, MYP or PYP.
Excellent communication skills in English, at a native speaker level.
The ability to establish rapport with adults and students. 
The ability to work effectively in a team.
The ability to function effectively under pressure. 
The ability to show initiative and work independently. 
A pleasant and friendly personality.

Experience working with students from diverse cultures and countries would be an advantage. In addition, there may be a possibility to increase the employment percentage if a candidate can teach other subjects and take on other responsibilities. 

At Stockholm International School we are committed to protecting children. Aligned with the recommendations of the International Task Force on Child Protection, we hold ourselves to a high standard of effective recruiting practices with specific attention to child protection. All applicants will therefore be required to undergo appropriate child protection screening. Included in the recruitment process will be a local and national police check as well as a mandatory police background check for the last 10 years of employment in every country worked. A judicial background check will be conducted prior to the issuance of the contract for prospective candidates applying to work at our school.
What we offer:
As well as the exciting opportunities this role presents, we also offer benefits in terms of; a pension scheme (Alecta ITP 1/ITP2), a generous wellness stipend, other insurances, and a substantial amount of professional development opportunities inside and outside the school. We also offer staff events and social gatherings that bring colleagues together, for example, hobby evenings and choir practices. Our locations in central Stockholm are easily accessible by public transportation.
Contract:
Employment Type: Parental Leave Replacement
Part-time, 80 %.
Start: January 7th, 2027
End: February 27th, 2027
Salary: Salary scale
Application:
Please email a short statement of interest as well as a current CV to: application@intsch.se. Mark the email with “French teacher Cover 80%”. We only accept applications in English and from qualified teachers. 
Applications will no longer be accepted after November 20th.
SIS reserves the right to close the application process when a suitable candidate is found.
